item.title: Shai-Hulud npm Worm Legacy and Public Linux Root Exploits
item.content:encoded:
Window: 18 Sep 18:00 → 18 Sep 22:00 UTC (4 hours)

Happy Birthday, Shai-Hulud — Should Read

One year after the first npm Shai-Hulud compromise, its credential-stealing, self-propagating supply-chain technique has evolved into repeated waves run by multiple actors, aided by publicly released code and CI token hijacking. Although two alleged TeamPCP members were arrested, the original worm’s authors remain unidentified and the threat persists across the npm ecosystem.

  • A malicious version of @ctrl/tinycolor published to npm in September 2025 initiated the first known self-propagating worm in the npm ecosystem, which spread into dozens of packages and CrowdStrike’s npm namespace.
  • The Shai-Hulud payload used TruffleHog to find npm tokens, GitHub credentials, and cloud keys, sent discovered secrets to attacker-controlled locations, added a GitHub Actions workflow for persistence, and republished itself using stolen npm tokens.
  • A November 2025 wave moved execution to the pre-install step, introduced setup_bun.js and bun_environment.js, and included a fallback that could attempt to wipe a user’s home directory.
  • Later 2026 campaigns used publicly released Shai-Hulud source code, including a May burst that pushed more than 400 malicious versions across 172 packages by hijacking short-lived OIDC tokens from CI.
  • Australian Federal Police arrested two men in Western Australia on August 26, 2026 over alleged TeamPCP involvement, but the original authors of the September and November 2025 Shai-Hulud attacks remain unidentified.

Technologies: package-registry, source-control, ci-cd

Products: npm, github-actions, trufflehog

Vendors: github, crowdstrike, google

Public Exploits Released for Four Linux Kernel Flaws That Enable Local Root — Should Read

Public proof-of-concept exploits for four Linux kernel flaws—DirtyAH6, TUNderflow, PPPoEject, and DiagSpill—can allow local users to gain root access on unpatched systems. Organizations should install distribution updates containing all four fixes, as disabling unprivileged user namespaces only mitigates three of the flaws.

  • Researcher Asim Manizada released working proof-of-concept exploits for four Linux kernel flaws—DirtyAH6, TUNderflow, PPPoEject, and DiagSpill—that can allow a local user to gain root access.
  • All four flaws have been fixed by Linux kernel maintainers, but systems running older kernels remain exposed now that exploit code is public.
  • DirtyAH6, TUNderflow, and PPPoEject require unprivileged user namespaces for an ordinary user to reach them, while DiagSpill requires no user namespaces if the SCTP networking module is available.
  • The first stable Linux kernel versions stated to contain the complete set of fixes are 5.10.270, 5.15.221, 6.1.188, 6.6.157, 6.12.109, 6.18.50, and 7.2.4.
  • The article says there are no reports that these flaws have been used in real-world attacks, and the released exploits are tuned to specific kernel builds and may crash systems.

Technologies: operating-system

Products: linux-kernel, open-vswitch

Vendors: linux-kernel-project, open-vswitch

item.title: WordPress Click2Shell, Gyazo Breach, and Transparent Tribe RapidRust Campaign
item.content:encoded:
Window: 18 Sep 14:00 → 18 Sep 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

Gyazo server flaw exploited to steal 23.6 million user records — Must Read

Gyazo disclosed that attackers exploited a server flaw on September 11, 2026, stealing roughly 23.6 million user records and metadata for 490 million images. Exposed data may include password hashes, session IDs, X tokens, and private-image details, so users should change reused passwords.

  • Gyazo said attackers exploited a server vulnerability on September 11, 2026, and accessed its database, exposing approximately 23.62 million user records.
  • The company detected suspicious activity on September 12 and said it fixed the vulnerability used in the incident.
  • Exposed user data may include names or nicknames, email addresses, password hashes, user and device IDs, login session IDs, X integration tokens, Google SSO email addresses, profile details, and subscription-related information.
  • Gyazo said the incident also exposed 490 million image metadata records, including image IDs, upload IP addresses, browser-identification strings, location data embedded in images, extracted text, titles, source URLs, and hashed passphrases for private images.
  • Gyazo temporarily suspended its service and disabled access to files whose records were exposed, while advising users to change passwords reused on other platforms and to watch for suspicious communications.

Technologies: cloud-platform

Products: gyazo, cosense

Vendors: helpfeel, google, x

New WordPress Click2Shell Flaw Forces Theme Installs, Can Chain to Code Execution — Should Read

WordPress patched the Click2Shell flaw, which lets a crafted link force a logged-in administrator’s browser to install and preview an inactive theme from WordPress.org. When chained with a separate vulnerable theme, the issue can lead to server-side code execution, so site owners should update to WordPress 7.1.1 or the applicable supported security release.

  • WordPress released security updates, including WordPress 7.1.1, to fix Click2Shell, a flaw that can cause a logged-in administrator who opens a crafted link to install and preview an inactive theme from WordPress.org.
  • The core Click2Shell flaw cannot install an arbitrary theme ZIP by itself; it installs a legitimate theme selected by the attacker from the official WordPress.org directory.
  • Pwn.ai demonstrated that Click2Shell could be chained with a separate flaw in the Mobile Repair Zone theme to run attacker-controlled code on the server.
  • The forced-installed theme remains inactive, so the site’s appearance does not change, but WordPress’s Customizer can load a theme’s PHP code while preparing a preview.
  • The article states that no evidence shows Click2Shell has been used in real attacks, and that updating WordPress core closes the demonstrated attack.

Technologies: cms

Products: wordpress, mobile-repair-zone

Vendors: wordpress, pwn-ai

Transparent Tribe Deploys New Rust Backdoor Using Private GitHub Repositories for C2 — Should Read

Pakistan-aligned Transparent Tribe (APT36) is targeting Indian and Afghan government and defense entities with a new Rust-based toolset, including the RUSTYSHADE backdoor. The campaign uses private GitHub repositories for encrypted command-and-control, USB propagation, and Windows/Linux file stealers to collect and exfiltrate data.

  • Pakistan-aligned Transparent Tribe, also known as APT36 and Earth Karkaddan, targeted government and defense entities in India and Afghanistan in an activity Zscaler calls Operation RapidRust.
  • The campaign uses four previously undocumented tools: the Rust-based RUSTYSHADE backdoor, the RUSTYMOVE USB propagation utility, and the PSNATCH and BASHNATCH file stealers for Windows and Linux.
  • RUSTYSHADE uses attacker-controlled private GitHub repositories and the GitHub REST API for encrypted two-way communications, including commands, results, system information, screenshots, webcam captures, and stolen files.
  • The attackers registered typosquatted domains resembling The Print and India Today to host malicious PowerShell scripts and payloads.
  • RUSTYMOVE monitors removable drives and copies a ZIP archive containing RUSTYSHADE and a disguised shortcut file to each detected drive.

Technologies: source-control, operating-system

Products: github, windows, powershell

Vendors: github, microsoft, zscaler

Fake LastPass Authenticator GitHub repos push new Rapuncel infostealer — Should Read

SEO-optimized fake GitHub repositories impersonating LastPass and dozens of other brands are distributing the new Rapuncel infostealer, alongside a Microsoft-signed kernel driver that can disable 145 antivirus and EDR products. Users should download software only from official sources and avoid promoted or suspicious search results.

  • SEO-optimized fake GitHub repositories impersonating LastPass and at least 39 other companies distribute the previously undocumented Rapuncel information stealer.
  • Victims are redirected from fake download buttons to ZIP archives inflated to as much as 148 MB, which contain a renamed Microsoft Visual Studio CoreCLR Debugger configured to load a malicious DLL.
  • The campaign deploys a Microsoft-signed Alinubx.sys kernel driver disguised as an NVIDIA component that is designed to terminate 145 antivirus and endpoint-detection processes.
  • Rapuncel steals credentials from 25 browsers, data from 30 cryptocurrency wallets, Discord, Steam, and Telegram session credentials, Windows Credential Manager contents, selected documents, screenshots, and system information.
  • Rapuncel persists through a Windows service and uploads compressed stolen data to 2.26.126[.]50 using an HTTP-formatted request over raw TCP.

Technologies: mfa, source-control, operating-system, browser

Products: lastpass-authenticator, github, windows, visual-studio-coreclr-debugger, google-chrome, microsoft-edge

Vendors: lastpass, github, microsoft, google

Nations take action on North Korean IT workers after UN report — Should Read

Countries including Argentina, Pakistan, Vietnam and Laos have taken legal, financial and investigative action against networks helping North Korean IT workers evade sanctions and earn foreign currency. A UN monitoring report says the scheme remains globally extensive, with China and Russia hosting most North Korean overseas workers despite increased scrutiny.

  • A UN-linked monitoring report says Argentina, Pakistan, Vietnam, and Laos took meaningful steps by July to address North Korean IT worker activities identified in an October report.
  • Argentina investigated Antonia Doroganova over allegations that she helped launder North Korean IT workers’ earnings, while Pakistan opened a case involving alleged provider of fraudulent identification documents Syeda Aliya Batool Zaidi and investigated two other alleged facilitators.
  • The report says Chinese authorities increased surveillance of North Korean IT workers and that their ability to enter China had become difficult as of July 2025.
  • The monitoring team estimates that at least 17 countries continue to host about 100,000 North Korean workers, with an estimated 20,000 to 70,000 in China and up to 30,000 in Russia.
  • North Koreans working outside the country generated up to $800 million last year, much of it through the IT worker scheme.

Teaching a Machine to Think Like an Incident Researcher — Optional

Varonis describes how its AI-powered Triage Agent investigates security alerts using data context, behavioral baselines, and adaptive evidence gathering to reconstruct incidents before human review. The company reports that the agent improves triage efficiency, prioritizes confirmed threats with over 96% recall, and reduces escalation time for malicious cases.

  • Varonis built its Triage Agent to investigate alerts end to end by gathering context about identities, permissions, sensitive data, behavior, and related events before a human analyst opens a case.
  • The agent uses normalized data, behavioral baselines, and more than 300 investigation scenarios to begin with relevant evidence and expand its investigation when needed.
  • In a production case, the agent linked three download-alert windows involving a sales employee, totaling more than 17,000 sensitive-file downloads from an anonymous consumer VPN endpoint.
  • The agent classified the linked activity as malicious and critical but noted that unavailable authentication telemetry prevented it from determining whether the activity involved stolen credentials, a hijacked session, or a deliberate insider.
  • Varonis states that the agent has improved analyst efficiency by 35% to 100%, reduced malicious-case escalation time by an average of 16.4 hours, and achieved production recall above 96%.

Technologies: dlp, iam

Products: varonis-triage-agent, varonis-data-security-platform, varonis-mddr

Vendors: varonis

What scales when headcount doubles — Optional

As organizations grow, IT operations must replace person-dependent processes with scalable systems, partners, and deliberate workflows for support, identity, compliance, and device logistics. The presentation shares practical lessons on deciding what to automate or operationalize while maintaining consistent employee experiences across regions.

  • As headcount grows, IT teams face rising ticket volume, more difficult identity and access management, increasingly complex compliance requirements, outdated documentation, and device operations that become logistical challenges.
  • Processes that depend on one person’s judgment or memory are likely failure points as an organization scales.
  • Tools commonly automate the well-defined middle of a process while leaving edge tasks such as forecasting, sourcing, storing, shipping, retrieving, and retiring devices unresolved.
  • Joe Hurshman of Teamworks will discuss decisions about which operations to build systems for, hand off to partners, or leave manual, based on experience at Teamworks, Found, and Apple.
  • The presentation includes an attendee question-and-answer section focused on specific real-world scaling challenges.

Technologies: operating-system, iam

Products: macos

Vendors: teamworks, apple

Detecting Data Exfiltration Before It Becomes a Breach | Corelight — Optional

Corelight promotes network-based detection and investigation capabilities to identify suspicious data exfiltration early, before it escalates into a breach.

  • The article is titled "Detecting Data Exfiltration Before It Becomes a Breach."
  • The article focuses on detecting data exfiltration before it develops into a breach.
  • Corelight is identified as the source of the article.

Technologies: network-monitoring

Products: corelight-open-ndr

Vendors: corelight

Secure enterprise sharing with access reviews for Microsoft 365 — Optional

Sponsored content promotes tenfold’s identity and access governance platform as a way to centrally monitor Microsoft 365 sharing and have data owners review or revoke stale access to Teams, SharePoint, and OneDrive files.

  • The article states that organizations using Microsoft 365 can lose visibility into who has access to files shared through Teams, SharePoint, and OneDrive.
  • It cites a Wire survey in which 61% of security leads said access to shared files often remains active longer than intended, while more than one-third reported difficulty identifying who can access sensitive shared files.
  • Microsoft 365’s sharing-link reports show new links over the previous 28 days, while site-level reports provide CSV lists of shared files and their users but can be time-consuming to run and review across an organization.
  • The article says access reviews should involve the people who originally shared files, because they can determine whether access is still needed.
  • The sponsored article promotes tenfold’s centralized reporting and owner-led access reviews for shared content in Microsoft cloud and on-premises environments.

Technologies: iam, cloud-platform

Products: tenfold, microsoft-365, sharepoint, onedrive, microsoft-teams

Vendors: tenfold-software, microsoft

item.title: Microsoft CVE-2026-85889 Patch, NightEagle Expansion, and AI Agent Supply-Chain Risks
item.content:encoded:
Window: 18 Sep 10:00 → 18 Sep 14:00 UTC (4 hours)

Hacking group ‘NightEagle’ targeting China’s high-tech sector expands operations to Russia — Should Read

NightEagle (APT-Q-95), a cyberespionage group previously focused on China’s high-tech and defense sectors, has expanded to target Russian organizations. Kaspersky says the group uses stolen VPN credentials, Microsoft Exchange backdoor GhostContainer, and Active Directory abuse to persist, move laterally, and pursue domain controllers.

  • Kaspersky reported that NightEagle, also known as APT-Q-95, expanded from its previous focus in Asia to target Russian businesses over the past year.
  • The group commonly used stolen credentials to enter corporate networks through VPNs, then targeted Microsoft Exchange servers and deployed the GhostContainer backdoor.
  • GhostContainer enables remote control of compromised servers, can evade some Windows security and logging mechanisms, and can redirect network traffic.
  • The attackers abused weaknesses in Active Directory to obtain higher privileges, move across networks, steal credentials, impersonate users, and attempt to compromise domain controllers.
  • QiAnXin previously reported that the group had targeted Chinese organizations in defense, semiconductors, artificial intelligence, and quantum technology since at least 2023.

Technologies: identity-provider, iam, operating-system, source-control

Products: microsoft-exchange-server, active-directory, windows, github

Vendors: kaspersky, qianxin, microsoft, github

Microsoft Patches CVSS 10.0 Azure AI Foundry Flaw Enabling Unauthorized Privilege Escalation — Should Read

Microsoft fixed CVE-2026-85889, a CVSS 10.0 Azure AI Foundry authentication flaw that could have allowed remote unauthorized privilege escalation; the cloud-service fix was applied automatically with no customer action required. It also addressed several other high-severity Azure, Microsoft 365 Copilot, and Windows privilege-escalation issues.

  • Microsoft patched CVE-2026-85889, a CVSS 10.0 Azure AI Foundry flaw caused by missing authentication that could allow an unauthorized network attacker to elevate privileges.
  • Microsoft credited researcher Rémy Marot with reporting CVE-2026-85889 and said there is no evidence that it has been exploited in the wild.
  • Microsoft also mitigated critical cloud vulnerabilities affecting Microsoft 365 Copilot, Azure Database for PostgreSQL, and Azure Cosmos DB, and said customers need take no action for these cloud-based issues.
  • An out-of-band Windows 11 version 26H1 update, KB5129194, addresses CVE-2026-62721 in Windows User-Mode Power Service and CVE-2026-85921 in Windows Secure Kernel Mode.
  • Microsoft recently patched 974 vulnerabilities across its portfolio, including actively exploited flaws affecting Windows Advanced Local Procedure Call and the Windows Update Stack.

Technologies: cloud-platform, database, operating-system, browser

Products: azure-ai-foundry, microsoft-365-copilot, azure-database-for-postgresql, azure-cosmos-db, windows-11, windows-user-mode-power-service, windows-secure-kernel-mode, google-chrome

Vendors: microsoft, google

WeaselBiscuit Stealer Spreads via 13 npm Packages to Harvest Chrome Extension Storage — Should Read

Researchers found 13 malicious npm packages distributing WeaselBiscuit, a lightweight JavaScript stealer that harvests Chrome extension storage across Windows, macOS, and Linux and can log keystrokes and clipboard data on Windows. The malware resembles DPRK-linked Contagious Interview tools such as BeaverTail and OtterCookie, but attribution to North Korea remains unconfirmed.

  • Researchers identified 13 npm packages that distribute a previously undocumented JavaScript information stealer named WeaselBiscuit.
  • When an affected npm package is imported, its loader retrieves the main WeaselBiscuit code from an Npoint URL and runs it in memory.
  • WeaselBiscuit collects Chrome extension storage on Windows, macOS, and Linux, including readable nonempty files in the Local Extension Settings directory.
  • On Windows systems, commands from its control server can direct WeaselBiscuit to record clipboard contents and keystrokes.
  • The malware shares functional and operational similarities with DPRK-associated BeaverTail and OtterCookie tooling, but researchers said there is no definitive evidence attributing WeaselBiscuit to North Korea.

Technologies: package-registry, browser

Products: npm, google-chrome, npoint

Vendors: github, google

Plugin4Shell Lets Repository Owners Swap Pinned Plugin Code Across Four AI Coding Agents — Should Read

Plugin4Shell lets owners of plugin repositories on certain Git hosts replace supposedly commit-pinned AI coding-agent plugins with malicious code because the agents do not verify the checked-out commit. Claude Code and OpenAI Codex have fixes, GitHub Copilot reportedly does not, and Google’s retiring Gemini CLI will not be patched.

  • Air Security reported that Plugin4Shell can let a plugin repository owner replace an AI coding agent’s commit-pinned plugin with different code because the agents do not verify that the installed code matches the requested commit.
  • The reported flaw affects Anthropic Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, and Google Gemini CLI, although the branch-name technique does not work on GitHub because GitHub blocks branch and tag names that resemble commit hashes.
  • A malicious swapped plugin could access the files, saved credentials, and reachable systems of the person running the AI coding agent.
  • Air Security said Claude Code was fixed in version 2.1.179 and OpenAI Codex in version 0.146.0, while GitHub Copilot had no fix and Google reportedly will not patch the retiring Gemini CLI.
  • The article says default Claude Code and Copilot plugin marketplaces were GitHub-based as of September 18, while the risk described by Air applies to supported code hosts such as Bitbucket or private Git servers that permit hash-like branch names.

Technologies: source-control

Products: claude-code, openai-codex, github-copilot, gemini-cli, antigravity, github, bitbucket, git

Vendors: anthropic, openai, github, microsoft, google, atlassian, air-security

One Dell Order, Two Companies, One Signature — Should Read

Attackers turned a genuine Dell order acknowledgement into a callback-phishing lure by placing a fraudulent order, then relaying the vendor-signed email through Microsoft 365 tenants to unrelated targets. DKIM and DMARC passed because the message was authentic, but its signed recipient field showed it was originally addressed to an attacker-controlled mailbox—not the final recipient.

  • Attackers submitted a Dell order using an attacker-controlled Microsoft 365 mailbox, causing Dell to generate and sign a genuine order acknowledgement and PDF.
  • The same signed message was relayed through different second-hop Microsoft 365 tenants to two unrelated organizations about two minutes apart, while its signature, message identifier, attachment hash, and purchase identifier remained identical.
  • The final messages passed sender-policy, DKIM, DMARC, and composite authentication checks because relaying changed the delivery envelope without altering the signed message content.
  • The signed recipient field still named the attacker-controlled tenant rather than the final recipient, providing evidence that the message was not originally generated for the receiving mailbox.
  • The order’s shipping and billing address fields contained a helpline phone number and sales-language text, making the phone number the only actionable content in an otherwise genuine Dell receipt.

Technologies: cloud-platform, email-security

Products: microsoft-365, adaptive-ai

Vendors: dell, microsoft, ironscales

A Vault with a Heap-View: The Uncomfortable Space Between AgentCore Harness and Identity — Should Read

Unit 42 found that AWS AgentCore Harness’s default shell tool can be abused through prompt injection to read the harness process memory and exfiltrate plaintext credentials resolved from AgentCore Identity. Operators should restrict allowed tools per invocation, minimize downstream service-account privileges, and tightly monitor or limit harness egress.

  • Unit 42 reported that AWS AgentCore Harness sessions include built-in shell and file-operations tools by default unless operators restrict them with the allowedTools parameter.
  • In the researchers’ test environment, the harness shell tool ran as root and could read the memory of the harness runtime process, where AgentCore Identity had resolved a downstream service credential into plaintext.
  • Using an indirect prompt injection embedded in a simulated support ticket, the researchers caused the agent to run a script that extracted an Amazon Cognito JWT and an MCP server URL from runtime memory and sent them to a controlled webhook.
  • The exfiltrated JWT belonged to the operator’s MCP service account rather than the end user and was replayed from a laptop to access simulated customer information through the downstream MCP server.
  • AWS closed the disclosure as informative under its AgentCore shared-responsibility model and cited allowedTools scoping and egress filtering as customer-side controls.

Technologies: cloud-platform, iam, secrets-manager

Products: amazon-bedrock-agentcore-harness, amazon-bedrock-agentcore-identity, amazon-cognito, cortex-cloud

Vendors: amazon-web-services, palo-alto-networks

Auditing in the age of (good enough) AI — May Read

Trail of Bits used AI agents to build MASM developer tooling, static analysis, and Lean formal models ahead of its Miden VM audit, substantially improving review coverage. The work uncovered a high-severity underconstrained prover-input flaw that could enable Falcon signature forgery, along with additional correctness bugs.

  • Trail of Bits spent six months preparing to audit the Miden VM by using AI agents to build a MASM language server, decompiler, static-analysis engine, and Lean model of the VM executor.
  • The static-analysis work identified more than 400 reachable locations in the Miden core library where type validation could be improved.
  • A high-severity flaw in the mod_12289 procedure failed to validate a prover-supplied remainder, allowing a malicious prover to return an incorrect result and potentially forge Falcon signatures to drain Miden accounts controlled by Falcon key pairs.
  • AI-assisted formal modeling produced 95 machine-checked correctness proofs covering all binary arithmetic components of the Miden core library.
  • The formal verification work found two additional bugs: an edge case in 64-bit right rotation and a 256-bit multiplication routine that removed caller-owned stack values before returning.

Products: miden-vm, miden-assembly, masm-lsp, masm-decompiler, masm-analysis, masm-lean

Vendors: trail-of-bits, miden

Microsoft fixes bug behind ‘Defender Antivirus is turned off’ alerts — May Read

Microsoft fixed a bug that falsely warned users that Defender Antivirus was turned off even when it was functioning correctly. The fix is included in Microsoft Defender Antivirus version 4.18.26080.4, released September 17.

  • Microsoft resolved a bug that generated false notifications claiming Microsoft Defender Antivirus was turned off even when it was active and functioning correctly.
  • The fix was delivered in Microsoft Defender Antivirus version 4.18.26080.4, released on September 17.
  • The issue affected all supported Windows client and server versions, including Windows 11 26H1 and Windows Server 2025.
  • The incorrect notifications could appear at Windows startup and intermittently afterward, and persisted even when notification settings were disabled.
  • Microsoft had acknowledged the issue in late August, after reports indicated it had affected Windows Insider Release Preview users since at least June.

Technologies: antivirus, operating-system

Products: microsoft-defender-antivirus, windows-security, windows-11, windows-server-2025

Vendors: microsoft

An Abandoned CDN Domain Was Re-Registered. Thousands of Sites Still Call It. — Optional

An expired CDN domain was re-registered while thousands of websites still referenced its subdomains, giving its new owner potential control over content loaded in visitors’ browsers. The article argues that CSP reporting can reveal and monitor third-party scripts and unauthorized client-side changes, particularly for PCI DSS compliance.

  • In July 2025, a previously expired domain used by a discontinued content delivery network was re-registered, while thousands of websites, code repositories, and documentation pages still contained hard-coded references to its hostnames.
  • Because the new owner has wildcard DNS control over the domain, they control what content any of its subdomains can now serve to sites that still load assets from them.
  • The article cites the June 2024 ownership change of polyfill.io, after which the domain served conditional redirects to mobile visitors despite being embedded on more than 110,000 sites.
  • Third-party scripts run in visitors’ browsers with the same access as a site’s own code and can read page content, form input, cookies, and local storage or send requests elsewhere.
  • The article says Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only can collect reports on code and connections that a policy would block without blocking or changing website behavior.

Products: report-uri

Vendors: report-uri

Webinar: Which Google Workspace security controls actually matter? — Optional

BleepingComputer and Material Security will host a September 23, 2026 webinar examining real Google Workspace breaches, including social-engineering and malicious OAuth app attacks. The session aims to help lean security teams prioritize the controls and incident-response measures with the greatest practical impact.

  • BleepingComputer will host a live webinar with Material Security on September 23, 2026, titled "Breach autopsy: How fast-growing companies are breached through Google Workspace."
  • Rajan Kapoor of Material Security and Rick Fitzgerald of Fireside Consulting LLC will examine publicly documented Google Workspace breaches.
  • The webinar will discuss two incidents in which social engineering and malicious OAuth applications were used to access Google Workspace environments.
  • Speakers will evaluate which Google Workspace controls offer the greatest value, which may be overrated, and how to prioritize improvements by effort and potential impact.
  • The discussion will also cover the first hours after breach discovery and response decisions that can limit or worsen an incident's impact.

Technologies: cloud-platform, iam

Products: google-workspace

Vendors: google, material-security

item.title: Check Point CVE-2026-91843 Root RCE and RatHat Android Persistence
item.content:encoded:
Window: 18 Sep 06:00 → 18 Sep 10:00 UTC (4 hours)

New Check Point flaw lets hackers execute code with root privileges — Should Read

Check Point patched CVE-2026-91843, a critical stack-based buffer overflow in Security Management Server and Log Server login handling that can give unauthenticated attackers root-level remote code execution. Organizations should apply the LivePatch promptly or restrict trusted clients and monitor for "Username too long" failed-login alerts.

  • Check Point released security updates for CVE-2026-91843, a critical stack-based buffer overflow in the login process of Security Management Server instances and Log Server systems.
  • CVE-2026-91843 can allow unprivileged attackers to execute code remotely with root privileges through a low-complexity attack that requires no user interaction.
  • Check Point said customers unable to deploy the LivePatch can harden vulnerable systems and restrict SmartConsole trusted-client access to approved IP addresses or subnets.
  • Check Point said potential CVE-2026-91843 attempts can be identified through "Administrator failed to log in: Username too long" alerts in Audit and Admin login logs.
  • The company has not flagged CVE-2026-91843 as actively exploited, but the Dutch NCSC warned that exploitation of the separate CVE-2026-85102 and CVE-2026-85103 flaws is expected soon.

Technologies: firewall, vpn, network-monitoring

Products: security-management-server, log-server, smartconsole, security-gateway

Vendors: check-point

Claimed Bug Bounty Hunter Likely Used LLM to Build PhantomRaven npm Stealer — Should Read

CrowdStrike links the PhantomRaven npm campaign to a purported bug bounty hunter who likely used an LLM to create a JavaScript stealer that harvested developer credentials, CI/CD secrets, and system data. The actor allegedly used malicious npm and PyPI packages to compromise targets and identify vulnerabilities for bounty claims.

  • CrowdStrike assessed with high confidence that the PhantomRaven JavaScript information stealer was likely written using a large language model, citing verbose comments, placeholder code, and token-analysis patterns.
  • Koi Security and DCODX first reported PhantomRaven in late October 2025 after identifying more than 100 malicious npm packages that used typosquatting and slopsquatting to target developers.
  • The malicious packages retrieved code from an external server and collected authentication tokens, CI/CD secrets, GitHub credentials, system details, and configuration information.
  • CrowdStrike linked the operation to a purported bug bounty hunter active since November 2022 and found no evidence that stolen information had appeared in stealer-log shops.
  • The actor also attempted to upload similar information-stealing code to PyPI, and two associated npm accounts that distributed PhantomRaven were no longer accessible.

Technologies: package-registry, ci-cd, source-control

Products: phantomraven, npm-registry, python-package-index, github-actions, gitlab-ci, jenkins, circleci

Vendors: crowdstrike, npm, pypi, github, gitlab, jenkins, circleci

RatHat Android Malware Abuses ADB to Retain Shell Access After Uninstall — Should Read

Researchers identified RatHat, an Android malware attributed to China-based actors that abuses Accessibility permissions and wireless ADB pairing to gain persistent shell access even after the malicious app is uninstalled. It uses AI-assisted device navigation, credential overlays, SMS interception, screen recording, and reverse tunnels for remote control.

  • Researchers at Zimperium identified RatHat, an Android malware assessed to be operated by China-based threat actors and distributed through smishing, malvertising, deceptive download portals, and third-party forums.
  • RatHat abuses Android Accessibility permissions to unlock Developer Options, enable Wireless Debugging, and obtain a six-digit Android Debug Bridge pairing code.
  • After gaining local Android Debug Bridge access, RatHat can run a Go-based agent and establish a reverse tunnel through FRP, allowing attackers to retain shell access even if the malicious app is uninstalled.
  • The malware can display credential-stealing overlays, record the screen, intercept SMS messages, collect device data and lock-screen credentials, capture keystrokes, and log screen touches.
  • RatHat sends the device’s Accessibility screen data to a generative AI assistant to identify on-screen text, locate targets for automated taps, and issue navigation actions such as scrolling.

Technologies: mobile-os, remote-access

Products: android, android-debug-bridge, frp

Vendors: google, zimperium, fatedier

Microsoft fixes broken copy and paste for Excel 2016 users — May Read

Microsoft released KB5002665 to fix silent copy-and-paste, autofill, and formula-dragging failures caused by the KB5002914 security update, but only for MSI-based Office 2016 installations. Users of other affected Excel versions should use Paste Special until a broader fix is available.

  • Microsoft confirmed that the September 2026 KB5002914 security update can cause certain Excel copy-and-paste operations, autofill, and formula dragging to fail silently because of a code regression.
  • Microsoft released KB5002665 to mitigate the issue for Microsoft Installer-based Office 2016 installations.

Gyazo server flaw exploited to steal 23.6 million user records — Must Read

Gyazo suffered a server vulnerability breach that exposed roughly 23.6 million user records and metadata for 490 million images, potentially including credentials, session tokens, and private-image information. The service was taken offline while Helpfeel investigates, and users should reset reused passwords.

  • Gyazo said attackers exploited a server vulnerability on September 11, 2026, and accessed its database containing approximately 23.62 million user records.
  • The exposed user information may include names or nicknames, email addresses, password hashes, user and device IDs, login session IDs, X integration tokens, Google SSO email addresses, profile details, subscription information, billing status, and usage statistics.
  • Gyazo said 490 million image metadata records were exposed, mostly for images uploaded before January 2019, including image IDs, upload IP addresses, User-Agent strings, EXIF location data, OCR-extracted text, image titles, source URLs, and hashed passphrases for private images.
  • Gyazo temporarily suspended its service and disabled access to files whose records were exposed because image IDs could potentially be used to access corresponding content.
  • Gyazo is notifying affected users directly and advises all users to change their passwords on Gyazo and any other platforms where they reused the same credentials.

Transparent Tribe Deploys New Rust Backdoor Using Private GitHub Repositories for C2 — Must Read

Pakistan-aligned Transparent Tribe (APT36) is targeting government and defense organizations in India and Afghanistan with new Rust-based tools, including the RUSTYSHADE backdoor. The campaign uses private GitHub repositories for encrypted command-and-control, alongside USB propagation and Windows/Linux file stealers.

  • Zscaler ThreatLabz attributed Operation RapidRust to Pakistan-aligned Transparent Tribe (APT36), which targeted government and defense entities in India and Afghanistan.
  • The campaign used four previously undocumented tools: the Rust-based RUSTYSHADE backdoor, the RUSTYMOVE USB propagation utility, and the PSNATCH and BASHNATCH file stealers.
  • RUSTYSHADE uses attacker-controlled private GitHub repositories and the GitHub REST API to receive encrypted commands, store system information, and send collected data.
  • PSNATCH and BASHNATCH collect files from Windows and Linux systems, while RUSTYMOVE copies staged malicious files to detected external removable drives.
  • The actors also registered domains impersonating The Print and India Today to host malicious PowerShell scripts and payloads.

Technologies: source-control, operating-system

Products: github, github-gist, windows, powershell

New Check Point flaw lets hackers execute code with root privileges — Should Read

Check Point patched CVE-2026-91843, a critical stack-based buffer overflow that can give unauthenticated attackers root remote code execution on Security Management Server and Log Server systems. Organizations should apply the LivePatch or restrict trusted-client access and monitor for “Username too long” failed-login alerts.

  • Check Point released security updates for CVE-2026-91843, a critical stack-based buffer overflow in the login process for Security Management Server instances.
  • The flaw also affects Check Point Log Server systems and can allow attackers without privileges to execute code remotely with root privileges without user interaction.
  • Customers unable to deploy the latest LivePatch can harden affected systems and restrict access to trusted IP addresses or subnets through SmartConsole.
  • Check Point said possible CVE-2026-91843 exploitation attempts can be identified through “Administrator failed to log in: Username too long” alerts in Audit and Admin login logs.
  • Check Point has not reported CVE-2026-91843 as actively exploited, but the Dutch National Cyber Security Centre warned that exploitation of the recently patched CVE-2026-85102 and CVE-2026-85103 flaws is expected soon.

North Korean hackers infect thousands of devices across 100 countries as part of ‘WaterPlum’ campaign — Should Read

A North Korean campaign dubbed WaterPlum infected at least 30,000 devices in 100 countries by posing as AI and blockchain recruiters, stealing more than $10.5 million and compromising roughly 7,000 cryptocurrency wallets. The operation also supports North Korea’s IT-worker schemes by retaining access to victims’ devices and potentially using stolen identities to infiltrate technology companies.

  • The WaterPlum campaign, attributed to North Korean cyber actors, infected at least 30,000 devices across 100 countries between December 2025 and July 2026.
  • The campaign stole more than $10.5 million and compromised funds or credentials from about 7,000 cryptocurrency wallets by targeting job seekers, particularly web designers, engineers, and cryptocurrency specialists.
  • WaterPlum actors posed as AI or blockchain companies and instructed applicants contacted through social media, gig-work sites, and freelance portals to download files during interviews.
  • Japanese police found BeaverTail, InvisibleFerret, OtterCookie, OtterCandy, and StoatWaffle malware variants on victims’ devices, along with tools used to steal information and maintain remote access.
  • Authorities linked WaterPlum to North Korea’s IT-worker schemes, including laptop farms and the use of stolen identities to obtain technology jobs.

Happy Birthday, Shai-Hulud — Should Read

One year after the first npm Shai-Hulud compromise, its credential-stealing, self-propagating supply-chain technique has evolved into repeated waves run by multiple actors, aided by publicly released code and CI token hijacking. Although two alleged TeamPCP members were arrested, the original worm’s authors remain unidentified and the threat persists across the npm ecosystem.

  • A malicious version of @ctrl/tinycolor published to npm in September 2025 initiated the first known self-propagating worm in the npm ecosystem, which spread into dozens of packages and CrowdStrike’s npm namespace.
  • The Shai-Hulud payload used TruffleHog to find npm tokens, GitHub credentials, and cloud keys, sent discovered secrets to attacker-controlled locations, added a GitHub Actions workflow for persistence, and republished itself using stolen npm tokens.
  • A November 2025 wave moved execution to the pre-install step, introduced setup_bun.js and bun_environment.js, and included a fallback that could attempt to wipe a user’s home directory.
  • Later 2026 campaigns used publicly released Shai-Hulud source code, including a May burst that pushed more than 400 malicious versions across 172 packages by hijacking short-lived OIDC tokens from CI.
  • Australian Federal Police arrested two men in Western Australia on August 26, 2026 over alleged TeamPCP involvement, but the original authors of the September and November 2025 Shai-Hulud attacks remain unidentified.

Products: npm, github-actions, trufflehog

Public Exploits Released for Four Linux Kernel Flaws That Enable Local Root — Should Read

Public proof-of-concept exploits for four Linux kernel flaws—DirtyAH6, TUNderflow, PPPoEject, and DiagSpill—can allow local users to gain root access on unpatched systems. Organizations should install distribution updates containing all four fixes, as disabling unprivileged user namespaces only mitigates three of the flaws.

  • Researcher Asim Manizada released working proof-of-concept exploits for four Linux kernel flaws—DirtyAH6, TUNderflow, PPPoEject, and DiagSpill—that can allow a local user to gain root access.
  • All four flaws have been fixed by Linux kernel maintainers, but systems running older kernels remain exposed now that exploit code is public.
  • DirtyAH6, TUNderflow, and PPPoEject require unprivileged user namespaces for an ordinary user to reach them, while DiagSpill requires no user namespaces if the SCTP networking module is available.
  • The first stable Linux kernel versions stated to contain the complete set of fixes are 5.10.270, 5.15.221, 6.1.188, 6.6.157, 6.12.109, 6.18.50, and 7.2.4.
  • The article says there are no reports that these flaws have been used in real-world attacks, and the released exploits are tuned to specific kernel builds and may crash systems.

New WordPress Click2Shell Flaw Forces Theme Installs, Can Chain to Code Execution — Should Read

WordPress patched Click2Shell in version 7.1.1, a flaw that lets a crafted link cause a logged-in administrator’s browser to install and preview an inactive WordPress.org theme. While the core bug alone cannot install arbitrary code, researchers chained it with a vulnerable theme to achieve server-side code execution, so site owners should update promptly.

  • WordPress released security updates, including WordPress 7.1.1, to fix Click2Shell, a flaw that can cause a logged-in administrator who opens a crafted link to install and preview an inactive theme from WordPress.org.
  • The Click2Shell core flaw does not accept an arbitrary theme ZIP, but pwn.ai demonstrated that it can be chained with a separate vulnerable theme to run attacker-controlled code on a server.
  • The researchers used the Mobile Repair Zone theme, whose background handler could download and run code from a supplied web address without checking permissions or a security token.
  • The forced-installed theme remains inactive, so the site’s appearance does not change, but WordPress can load a theme’s PHP code while creating a preview in its Customizer tool.
  • WordPress says supported branches back to 4.7 received fixes, and there is no indication that Click2Shell has been exploited in real-world attacks.

SEO-optimized fake GitHub repositories impersonating LastPass and dozens of other brands are distributing the Rapuncel infostealer, which uses a Microsoft-signed kernel driver to disable security products. Users should download software only from official sources and avoid promoted or dubious search results.

  • An ongoing campaign uses search-optimized fake GitHub repositories impersonating LastPass and at least 39 other companies to distribute the previously undocumented Rapuncel information stealer.
  • Victims who click download buttons on the fake repositories are redirected to servers that provide ZIP files inflated to as much as 148 MB, containing a renamed Microsoft Visual Studio CoreCLR Debugger configured to load a malicious DLL.

NightEagle (APT-Q-95), a cyberespionage group previously focused on China’s high-tech and defense sectors, has expanded to Russian organizations. Kaspersky reports it uses stolen VPN credentials, Microsoft Exchange compromise, and the GhostContainer backdoor to persist, steal credentials, and target domain controllers.

  • Kaspersky reported that NightEagle, also known as APT-Q-95, expanded from targeting organizations in Asia to targeting Russian businesses over the past year.
  • In most Russian incidents, the group used stolen credentials to access corporate networks through VPNs, then targeted Microsoft Exchange servers and installed the GhostContainer backdoor.
  • GhostContainer can remotely control compromised servers, evade some Windows security and logging mechanisms, and redirect network traffic.
  • After obtaining access, the attackers exploited Active Directory weaknesses to gain privileges, move across systems, steal credentials, impersonate users, and attempt to compromise domain controllers.

CrowdStrike links the PhantomRaven npm campaign to a purported bug bounty hunter who likely used an LLM to create a JavaScript stealer that harvested developer credentials, CI/CD secrets, and system data. The actor allegedly used malicious npm and PyPI packages to compromise targets and identify vulnerabilities for bounty claims.

  • CrowdStrike linked the operation to a purported bug bounty hunter active since November 2022 and found no evidence that stolen information had appeared in stealer-log shops.

Nations take action on North Korean IT workers after UN report — Should Read

A UN-linked monitoring team reports that countries including Argentina, Pakistan, Vietnam and Laos have taken legal or enforcement action against North Korean IT-worker networks that use fraudulent identities, local facilitators and financial accounts to generate revenue for Pyongyang. China has also increased scrutiny of the workers, constraining new deployments amid espionage-related arrests.

  • The Multilateral Sanctions Monitoring Team reported that Argentina, Pakistan, Vietnam and Laos took meaningful steps in response to allegations involving North Korean workers operating abroad.
  • Argentina opened an investigation into Antonia Doroganova over allegations that she helped launder money earned by North Korean IT workers, while Pakistan opened a case against Syeda Aliya Batool Zaidi over alleged provision of fraudulent identification documents.
  • The report said Chinese authorities have increased surveillance of North Korean IT workers, and that a worker was reportedly arrested in April 2025 for allegedly stealing Chinese military secrets.
  • The MSMT estimates that at least 17 countries continue to host about 100,000 North Korean workers, with an estimated 20,000 to 70,000 in China and up to 30,000 in Russia.
  • North Koreans working outside the country generated up to $800 million last year, much of it from the IT worker scheme, according to the report.

Microsoft has fixed a CVSS 10.0 Azure AI Foundry authentication flaw (CVE-2026-85889) that could have allowed unauthenticated network attackers to escalate privileges; the cloud service was fully mitigated and requires no customer action.

  • Microsoft patched CVE-2026-85889, a CVSS 10.0 Azure AI Foundry flaw caused by missing authentication for a critical function that could allow an unauthorized network attacker to elevate privileges.
  • Microsoft credited researcher Rémy Marot for reporting CVE-2026-85889 and said there is no evidence that it has been exploited in the wild.
  • Microsoft also mitigated critical cloud flaws affecting Microsoft 365 Copilot, Azure Database for PostgreSQL, and Azure Cosmos DB, and said these cloud vulnerabilities require no customer action.
  • An out-of-band Windows 11 version 26H1 update, KB5129194, addresses CVE-2026-62721 in Windows User-Mode Power Service and CVE-2026-85921 in Windows Secure Kernel Mode.

Technologies: cloud-platform, database, operating-system, browser

Vendors: microsoft, google

Plugin4Shell Lets Repository Owners Swap Pinned Plugin Code Across Four AI Coding Agents — Should Read

Plugin4Shell lets repository owners substitute malicious plugin code despite commit-hash pinning in Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, and Gemini CLI when plugins are hosted on Git servers that permit hash-like branch names. Claude Code and Codex have fixes, Copilot remains unpatched, and Google reportedly will not fix the retiring Gemini CLI.

  • Air Security reported that Plugin4Shell can let a plugin repository owner replace code installed by AI coding agents even when the plugin is pinned to a specific reviewed commit hash.
  • The issue affects Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, and Gemini CLI because their installers may accept a branch name made to resemble the pinned code identifier rather than verifying the downloaded code matches it.
  • GitHub blocks branch and tag names that look like commit hashes, so plugins from GitHub repositories are not exposed to the branch-name variant of the issue described by Air Security.
  • Anthropic reportedly fixed Claude Code in version 2.1.179 and OpenAI fixed Codex in version 0.146.0, while Air Security said GitHub Copilot has no fix and Google will not patch Gemini CLI.
  • A swapped plugin can run with the user’s access and could reach their files, saved credentials, and systems they can log in to.

Technologies: source-control, package-registry

Products: claude-code, codex, github-copilot, gemini-cli, antigravity, bitbucket

Vendors: anthropic, openai, github, google, air-security

One Dell Order, Two Companies, One Signature — Should Read

Attackers turned a genuine Dell order acknowledgement into a callback-phishing lure by placing a fraudulent order, then relaying the vendor-signed email through Microsoft 365 tenants to unrelated targets. DKIM and DMARC passed because the message was authentic, but its signed recipient field showed it was originally addressed to an attacker-controlled mailbox—not the final recipient.

  • Attackers submitted a Dell order using an attacker-controlled Microsoft 365 mailbox, causing Dell to generate and sign a genuine order acknowledgement and PDF.
  • The same signed message was relayed through different second-hop Microsoft 365 tenants to two unrelated organizations about two minutes apart, while its signature, message identifier, attachment hash, and purchase identifier remained identical.
  • The final messages passed sender-policy, DKIM, DMARC, and composite authentication checks because relaying changed the delivery envelope without altering the signed message content.
  • The signed recipient field still named the attacker-controlled tenant rather than the final recipient, providing evidence that the message was not originally generated for the receiving mailbox.
  • The order’s shipping and billing address fields contained a helpline phone number and sales-language text, making the phone number the only actionable content in an otherwise genuine Dell receipt.

Technologies: cloud-platform, email-security

Products: microsoft-365, adaptive-ai

Vendors: dell, microsoft, ironscales

RatHat Android Malware Abuses ADB to Retain Shell Access After Uninstall — Should Read

Researchers identified RatHat, an Android malware attributed to China-based actors that abuses Accessibility permissions and wireless ADB pairing to gain persistent shell access even after the malicious app is uninstalled. It uses AI-assisted device navigation, credential overlays, SMS interception, screen recording, and reverse tunnels for remote control.

  • Researchers at Zimperium identified RatHat, an Android malware assessed to be operated by China-based threat actors and distributed through smishing, malvertising, deceptive download portals, and third-party forums.
  • RatHat abuses Android Accessibility permissions to unlock Developer Options, enable Wireless Debugging, and obtain a six-digit Android Debug Bridge pairing code.
  • After gaining local Android Debug Bridge access, RatHat can run a Go-based agent and establish a reverse tunnel through FRP, allowing attackers to retain shell access even if the malicious app is uninstalled.
  • The malware can display credential-stealing overlays, record the screen, intercept SMS messages, collect device data and lock-screen credentials, capture keystrokes, and log screen touches.
  • RatHat sends the device’s Accessibility screen data to a generative AI assistant to identify on-screen text, locate targets for automated taps, and issue navigation actions such as scrolling.

Technologies: mobile-os, remote-access

Products: android, android-debug-bridge, frp

Vendors: google, zimperium, fatedier

Microsoft Teams will let admins block custom file extensions — Should Read

Microsoft Teams will begin rolling out customizable Weaponizable File Protection controls in November 2026, allowing administrators to choose which file extensions are blocked in chats and channels.

  • Microsoft Teams plans to let administrators customize the file extensions blocked by its Weaponizable File Protection feature.
  • Weaponizable File Protection scans Teams chats and channels and blocks messages containing dangerous, high-risk file attachments.
  • Microsoft says the customizable file-blocking controls are in development and are scheduled to begin rolling out in November 2026.
  • The feature will be available on Android, desktop, iOS, macOS, and web for standard multi-tenant cloud environments worldwide.
  • Microsoft is also adding Teams protections such as external-user blocking through the Defender portal, blurred QR codes from external senders, suspicious guest-invitation reporting, and automatic blocking of identified external bots from meetings.

Researchers found 13 malicious npm packages distributing the lightweight WeaselBiscuit JavaScript stealer, which harvests Chrome extension storage across Windows, macOS, and Linux and can log keystrokes and clipboard data on Windows. Its code and infrastructure overlap with DPRK-linked Contagious Interview tooling, though attribution to North Korea is not confirmed.

  • Researchers identified 13 npm packages that distribute a previously undocumented JavaScript information stealer called WeaselBiscuit.
  • Importing one of the malicious packages triggers a loader that retrieves the main malware from an Npoint URL and runs it directly in memory.
  • WeaselBiscuit collects Chrome extension storage on Windows, macOS, and Linux, including readable nonempty files in the Local Extension Settings directory.
  • Based on commands from its control server, WeaselBiscuit can record clipboard contents and keystrokes on Windows systems.
  • The malware overlaps with DPRK-associated BeaverTail and OtterCookie tooling, but researchers said there is not enough evidence to conclusively attribute it to North Korea.

Products: npm, google-chrome, npoint-io

Vendors: github, google

A Vault with a Heap-View: The Uncomfortable Space Between AgentCore Harness and Identity — Should Read

Unit 42 found that AWS AgentCore Harness’s default shell tool can be steered via prompt injection to run code as root, read the harness process memory, and extract plaintext credentials resolved from AgentCore Identity. Organizations should restrict allowedTools per invocation, apply least privilege to downstream service accounts, and tightly monitor or limit harness egress.

  • Unit 42 reported that AWS AgentCore Harness provides built-in shell and file-operation tools by default unless operators restrict them with the allowedTools parameter at invocation time.
  • In the researchers’ test environment, an indirect prompt injection embedded in a support ticket caused the harness to download and execute a script through its shell tool.
  • The researchers found that the shell tool ran as root and could read the memory of the harness runtime process, where AgentCore Identity credentials had been resolved into plaintext.
  • The test script extracted an Amazon Cognito bearer token and the connected MCP server URL from process memory, then sent them to a simulated attacker-controlled endpoint.
  • AWS closed the report as informative under its AgentCore shared-responsibility model and identified tool scoping and outbound-network filtering as customer-side controls.

Technologies: cloud-platform, iam, secrets-manager

Products: amazon-bedrock-agentcore-harness, amazon-bedrock-agentcore-identity, amazon-cognito, cortex-cloud

Vendors: amazon-web-services, palo-alto-networks

Auditing in the age of (good enough) AI — May Read

Trail of Bits used AI agents to build MASM developer tooling, static analyses, and Lean formal models before auditing the Miden zkVM, enabling deeper review of an unfamiliar assembly ecosystem. The work uncovered a critical underconstrained prover input that could enable Falcon signature forgery, plus additional correctness bugs, while producing 95 machine-checked proofs.

  • Trail of Bits spent six months preparing to audit the Miden VM by using AI agents to build MASM tooling, including an LSP server, decompiler, static-analysis engine, and Lean model of the VM executor.
  • The static analyses identified more than 400 reachable locations in the Miden core library where type validation could be improved.
  • A high-severity flaw in the mod_12289 procedure failed to validate a prover-supplied remainder, allowing a malicious prover to return an incorrect modular result and potentially forge Falcon signatures to steal funds from Miden accounts.
  • Trail of Bits generated 95 machine-checked Lean correctness proofs covering all binary arithmetic components of the Miden core library.
  • The formal-modeling work also found bugs in the 64-bit rotr procedure and the 256-bit wrapping_mul procedure that existing unit tests had not detected.

Vendors: trail-of-bits, miden, anthropic, openai, lean-fpl

Microsoft fixes bug behind ‘Defender Antivirus is turned off’ alerts — May Read

Microsoft fixed a bug that falsely warned users that Defender Antivirus was turned off even though protection remained active. The fix is included in Microsoft Defender Antivirus version 4.18.26080.4, released September 17.

  • Microsoft fixed a bug that incorrectly reported Microsoft Defender Antivirus as turned off even when it was operating normally.
  • The fix was delivered in Microsoft Defender Antivirus version 4.18.26080.4, released on September 17.
  • The erroneous Windows Security notifications affected supported Windows client and server versions, including Windows 11 26H1 and Windows Server 2025.
  • The false alerts could appear at Windows startup and intermittently afterward, and persisted even when notification settings were disabled.
  • Microsoft had acknowledged the issue in late August after reports indicated it had affected Windows Insider Release Preview users since at least June.

Microsoft fixes broken copy and paste for Excel 2016 users — May Read

Microsoft released KB5002665 to fix a KB5002914 regression that caused copy, paste, autofill, and formula dragging to fail silently in MSI-based Office 2016. Users of other affected Excel versions must use Paste Special or consider rolling back the security update, which removes important vulnerability patches.

  • Microsoft said the September 2026 KB5002914 security update introduced a code regression that can cause Excel copy-and-paste operations, autofill, and formula dragging to fail silently.
  • Microsoft released KB5002665 to address the issue for Microsoft Installer-based Office 2016, but the fix does not apply to Office 2016 Click-to-Run editions.

An expired CDN domain was re-registered while thousands of websites still load assets from its subdomains, giving its new owner potential control over content delivered to visitors. The article argues that browser-side CSP reporting and script monitoring are needed to detect third-party script changes that conventional server-side security tools may miss.

  • The new domain owner controls wildcard DNS for the domain, meaning any hostname under it now resolves to infrastructure they control.
  • The article cites the June 2024 Polyfill.io ownership change, after which the service began serving conditional redirects to mobile visitors despite being embedded on more than 110,000 sites.
  • Third-party scripts run in visitors’ browsers with the same access as first-party page code and can read page content, form fields, cookies, and local storage, as well as make outbound requests.

Zimperium discovered RatHat, an Android malware family that uses Accessibility permissions, wireless ADB, and AI-guided interface navigation to remotely control infected devices and steal banking credentials, SMS one-time passwords, and lock-screen secrets. It is distributed through malicious ads, SMS messages, and phishing sites that push APKs outside Google Play.

  • The malware can display fake banking and cryptocurrency app screens to steal credentials, intercept SMS messages and notifications containing one-time passwords, and capture lock-screen PINs, passwords, and unlock patterns.
  • RatHat sends a live map of the phone’s interface to an unnamed AI assistant, which returns element locations, text, and navigation instructions for adaptable remote control.

Critical Unbound DNSSEC Validator Flaw Could Allow RCE via a Malicious DNS Zone — Must Read

NLnet Labs released Unbound 1.26.1 to fix a critical DNSSEC validator heap overflow (CVE-2026-81642) that a malicious DNS zone could potentially use for remote code execution. All Unbound versions through 1.26.0 are affected, and administrators should upgrade or apply the vendor patches immediately.

  • NLnet Labs released Unbound 1.26.1 to fix CVE-2026-81642, a critical heap overflow in the DNSSEC validator affecting every Unbound release through 1.26.0.
  • An attacker controlling a malicious DNS zone can trigger CVE-2026-81642 by querying a vulnerable resolver, causing denial of service and potentially remote code execution through attacker-controlled data.
  • Unbound 1.26.1 also fixes eight additional flaws, including CVE-2026-82717, a heap corruption issue in CNAME synthesis that may permit remote code execution under certain systems and compilation options.
  • NLnet Labs provides standalone and combined source patches for organizations unable to upgrade, while stating that the standalone patches for CVE-2026-81642 and CVE-2026-82717 were tested on Unbound 1.26.0.
  • NLnet Labs reported no known exploitation of either potential code-execution flaw, and CISA marked exploitation of CVE-2026-81642 as none on Wednesday.

Products: unbound

Vendors: nlnet-labs

China-aligned FamousSparrow has shifted to a new modular C++ backdoor called SparroWocky, targeting government entities across Latin America since at least August 2025. The malware uses DLL sideloading, encrypted TLS command-and-control, and anti-analysis techniques to support espionage activities.

  • China-aligned threat actor FamousSparrow has deployed the previously unreported modular C++ backdoor SparroWocky in attacks against Latin American targets since at least August 2025.
  • ESET assessed that FamousSparrow has replaced SparrowDoor with SparroWocky as its primary implant and noted overlaps between the group, Earth Estries, and Salt Typhoon.
  • SparroWocky can execute files and commands, act as a TCP proxy, collect system and network information, exfiltrate files, take screenshots, perform file operations, and delete itself.
  • The backdoor uses DLL sideloading for execution and incorporates Mbed TLS, MinHook, COFF Loader, and a SilentMoonwalk variant for communications, in-memory plugins, and defense evasion.
  • Starting in July 2025, FamousSparrow primarily targeted high-profile government entities in Argentina, Ecuador, Guatemala, Honduras, Panama, Peru, Puerto Rico, and Venezuela, with 90% of its recorded targets located in Latin America.
